purpose: A route-constrained Extended Kalman Filter that provides dead-reckoning position along a known transit polyline when GPS is degraded or absent (tunnels, deep-metro segments). It fuses IMU (accelerometer/gyro) forward-acceleration with GPS fixes projected onto the route, plus ZUPT (zero-velocity) and station-snap corrections, to keep the app's wake-up alarm firing at the right station even with no satellite fix. It is the accuracy backbone behind SensorFusionManager and feeds an EkfPublicState (progress meters, velocity, sigma, mode) into the tracking/alarm pipeline. The whole subsystem is a 1-D filter on route arc-length s, not a 2-D lat/lng filter — geometry is handled by RouteGeometry projecting to/from meters.
responsibilities: Estimate 1-D route progress s (meters), velocity v (m/s), and accel bias b via a 3-state EKF (EkfPipeline) with predict/GPS-update/ZUPT/station-snap steps
Convert raw IMU samples into route-tangent forward acceleration using TiltFilter gravity/rotation and RouteGeometry.tangentAt, then drive prediction
Classify motion state (stationary/vehicle/human) from accel/gyro variance + FFT features and gate mode transitions (MotionClassifier, duration gate)
Detect GPS degradation and enter/exit degraded (dead-reckoning) mode with bounded covariance growth (GpsDegradationDetector + DegradedMode)
Detect zero-velocity intervals (ZuptDetector) and, on confirmation, apply ZUPT bias correction and attempt station association
Associate the current estimate to a discrete station and emit gated StationSnapConfirmed events (§24.2 confidence gate) consumed by ActiveRouteManager
Provide offline replay/test harnesses (ImuReplayEngineV2, EkfTestController, test_routes) that reproduce recorded/simulated rides byte-deterministically for the dashboard and integration tests

invariants: Filter operates in 1-D route arc-length meters (s), NOT lat/lng; all GPS enters via RouteGeometry.projectLatLng and exits via positionAt — a route MUST be set or the whole EKF is disabled (enableEkf = geometry != null)
publicState.s is monotonic non-decreasing in surface/metro modes (_sPub = max(_sPub,_s)); ONLY in degraded mode is raw internal _s exposed so DR isn't frozen by the monotonic clamp
EkfPipeline is uninitialized until the first GPS fix (_initializeFromGps); onForwardAccel/onZupt/onStation are no-ops before that — prediction is also gated by orchestrator._predictionEnabled
onStationCandidates applies an update ONLY when exactly one candidate is passed (candidates.length != 1 → return); StationAssociation enforces single-candidate selection
Accel bias b is observable only during ZUPT (k2 used) and via a weak GPS-derived-accel update (gain 0.05); GPS position and station-snap updates deliberately suppress the bias gain (k2 = 0)
IMU timestamps are Duration (monotonic since stream start); dt must fall in (0, maxDt=0.2]; larger/zero/negative dt skip integration to protect the covariance
sigmaS is clamped to a 200m ceiling (was 10km) so the station-association window (3σ+100m ≈ 700m) stays small enough to disambiguate adjacent stations
StationSnapConfirmed is emitted only through the §24.2 gate: σ_after_snap ≤ 30m (≤60m degraded) AND station index strictly greater than last snapped (monotonic)
gotchas: The header comment in ekf_orchestrator.dart says 'not yet integrated into app' — this is STALE. It is live-wired: location_stream_handler.dart passes enableEkf: geometry != null, so the EKF runs whenever an active route has ≥2 points.

EkfConfig has softGateSigma(3.0)/hardGateSigma(5.0)/stationSnapSigmaGate(30.0) fields that are NOT read by the code that matters: EkfPipeline hardcodes Huber thresholds 2.5σ/15σ, and the orchestrator hardcodes the snap gate 30m/60m. Editing EkfConfig will not change gating behavior.

RouteGeometry.projectLatLng returns NaN when lateral error exceeds maxLateralErrorMeters (75m surface / 50m transit) and onGpsFixAuto silently returns on NaN — off-route GPS fixes are dropped with no update, which can look like a stuck filter.

Two parallel replay engines exist: imu_replay_engine.dart (v1, 659 LOC, used only by dashboard/ekf_replay_panel.dart) and imu_replay_engine_v2.dart (v2, 2691 LOC, used by EkfTestController + integration tests). They are NOT interchangeable; new work should target v2.

Motion-state changes are deliberately slow: the duration gate (_motionStepSeconds=1.28s) requires 2 consecutive agreeing classifications, so a real stop/start takes ~2.5s to register — do not expect instantaneous stationary detection.

Degraded-mode covariance inflation is a per-tick factor of 1.0002 (~1%/s at 50Hz), tuned to keep σs under ~100m for ~3 minutes; changing it or the 200m clamp directly breaks station snaps (comments warn the old 1.02 / 10km values did).

The orchestrator maintains its own accel/gyro variance windows AND a static pre-GPS bias-init window (100–500 samples); this bias is subtracted from aFwd ONLY in degraded mode, so surface-mode DR does not get the same correction.

In non-metro (isMetroLeg=false) legs reverse motion is allowed; setStationContext(isMetroLeg:true) calls pipeline.setAllowReverse(false) which clamps v≥0 and s≥sOld — a mislabeled leg type silently changes filter dynamics.
MotionState enum here is {human, vehicle, stationary} and defaults to vehicle; do not confuse it with any app-level motion/transit-mode enums — this one lives in ekf_types.dart and is EKF-internal.

ekf_logger.dart exposes a global singleton `ekfLogger`; verbose logging (logVerbosity ≥1/2) is threaded through onLog callbacks and can be very chatty on the IMU tick path — keep verbosity at 0 for performance-sensitive runs.

purpose: The decision-and-delivery core of WakePoint's wake-up alarm. AlarmEvaluator is a stateless geometric state machine that decides WHEN to fire per route leg (stops / time / distance thresholds), classifies the trigger (destination, transfer, mode_change, final_station, preBoarding) and builds the user-facing message. NotificationService is the singleton that actually presents and persists the Android/iOS alarm, journey-progress and paused notifications, and brokers user actions (Stop Alarm / End Tracking / Mute / Resume) across isolates. StopLogicEngine is a mostly-pre-trip helper that validates whether the user's chosen stops threshold is achievable for the route; it is NOT in the runtime firing path.

purpose: The routing subsystem turns a Google Directions API response into the canonical route model the whole app tracks against: fetched/cached directions, per-leg transit stop geometry, transfer/mode-change event boundaries, step-level distance+duration boundaries for ETA, and a live "which route am I on" active-route state with automatic route switching. RouteSessionManager is the orchestrator (owned by TrackingService); TransferUtils is the pure-function toolbox that every alarm/tracking consumer imports (49 importers, the app's #1 fan-in hub) to reason about stops, legs, and events.
responsibilities: Fetch driving/transit directions with tiered in-memory + Hive caching and a metro-preference fallback (DirectionService.getDirections)
Group raw Directions steps into colored, mode-styled polyline segments for the map (DirectionService.buildRawSegments / buildSegmentedPolylines)
Extract per-transit-leg stop positions/meters/names and compute stops-passed/remaining (TransferUtils.extractTransitLegStops + TransitLegStops)

Compute transfer and mode-change event boundaries and step distance/duration boundaries in cumulative meters (TransferUtils.buildRouteEvents / buildStepBoundariesAndStops / buildTransferBoundariesMeters)
Orchestrate a multi-route session: registry, active-route selection, deviation monitoring, reroute policy, soft-lock, and per-route state maps (RouteSessionManager)
Continuously snap the user to the active route and auto-switch between candidate routes with sustain/blackout hysteresis (ActiveRouteManager.ingestPosition)
Simplify (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker) and gzip/base64 compress polylines (PolylineSimplifier)
Interpolate ETA-remaining and ETA-to-target seconds from step boundaries + durations (EtaUtils)
Persist raw Directions responses to disk for offline reconstruction/testing (RouteLogger)

keyFiles.role: Top fan-in hub (49 importers): TransitLegStops + RouteEventBoundary data models and the static TransferUtils toolbox for stops/legs/events/boundaries; pure functions over raw Directions JSON

Session orchestrator owned by TrackingService; owns RouteRegistry/ActiveRouteManager/DeviationMonitor/ReroutePolicy/SoftLockManager and all per-route *ByKey state; two registration paths (registerRouteFromDirections, registerRoute)
Directions fetch + 2-tier cache (in-memory TTL + Hive RouteCache) with metro-preference fallback; builds segmented polylines; DirectionService + ModeInfo
Live snap-to-active-route + hysteretic multi-route switching using monotonic Stopwatch timers; emits ActiveRouteState/RouteSwitchEvent/StationSnapConfirmed; EKF station-snap monotonic gate
RDP polyline simplification (tolerance in meters) + gzip/base64 compress/decompress
Stateless ETA math: etaRemainingSeconds and etaToTargetSeconds via linear interpolation across cumulative step boundaries + durations
Singleton RouteLogger.instance; writes full Directions JSON + summary to app documents route_logs/ on every fetch; enabled by default

publicSymbols: TransferUtils (static: extractTransitLegStops, buildRouteEvents, buildStepBoundariesAndStops, buildTransferBoundariesMeters, buildRouteSegments, countStopsPassed, countStopsRemaining, nStopsPriorTarget, firstTransitBoardingStops, enhanceTransitLegStopsWithOsm)
RouteEventBoundary (meters, type 'transfer'|'mode_change', label, lat, lng, associatedLegIndex)

RouteSessionManager.registerRouteFromDirections / registerRoute / switchToRoute / ingestPosition / clearSession; streams routeStateStream/routeSwitchStream/rerouteStream/deviationStateStream; per-route maps routeEventsByKey/stepBoundsMetersByKey/stepDurationsSecondsByKey/transitLegStopsByKey
ActiveRouteManager.ingestPosition / setActive / onStationSnapConfirmed / resetStationSnapIndex; streams stateStream/switchStream/stationSnapStream; ActiveRouteState; RouteSwitchEvent
dataFlow: TrackingService calls DirectionService.getDirections(lat/lng, transitMode, threshold) -> ApiClient hits backend; result cached in-memory (keyed by RouteCache.makeKey with the ACTUAL transitVariant/departureTime used) and in Hive RouteCache, logged via RouteLogger, overview polyline simplified (PolylineSimplifier.simplifyPolyline @10m) + compressed onto route['simplified_polyline']. TrackingService then calls RouteSessionManager.registerRouteFromDirections(directions, origin, destination, transitMode). RouteSessionManager derives key = RouteCache.makeKey(...), decodes points, and populates per-route maps: routeEventsByKey (TransferUtils.buildRouteEvents), stepBoundsMetersByKey + stepDurationsSecondsByKey (TransferUtils.buildStepBoundariesAndStops), transitLegStopsByKey (TransferUtils.extractTransitLegStops, optionally OSM-enhanced), then upserts a RouteEntry into RouteRegistry and lazily creates ActiveRouteManager/DeviationMonitor/ReroutePolicy. On each GPS fix RouteSessionManager.ingestPosition(position) -> ActiveRouteManager.ingestPosition(LatLng) -> SnapToRouteEngine.snap over registry entries, candidate offset/sustain/blackout hysteresis, emits ActiveRouteState{activeKey, snapped, progressMeters, remainingMeters, pendingSwitch...}. progressMeters feeds TransitLegStops.stopsPassed/stopsRemaining and EtaUtils.etaRemainingSeconds(progressMeters, stepBoundsMetersByKey[key], stepDurationsSecondsByKey[key]) which alarm/notification consumers read.
entryPoints: RouteSessionManager.registerRoute (lower-level intake from serialized payload / foreground-isolate restore)
invariants: Route identity is RouteCache.makeKey(origin, destination, mode, transitVariant[, departureTime]) everywhere; RouteSessionManager keys all per-route *ByKey maps and RouteRegistry entries by it, and DirectionService keys its caches by it
stepBoundariesMeters and stepDurationsSeconds must be equal length and boundaries strictly cumulative/ascending, or EtaUtils returns null
TransitLegStops: stopPositions.length == stopMeters.length == numStops, and stopMeters must be ascending (stopsPassed breaks on first unpassed stop)
TransitLegStops.legId must stay stable across reroutes/reparses for a given leg (drives one-alarm-per-leg dedupe like preBoarding); it deliberately avoids keying off dynamic inferred station names
ActiveRouteManager uses monotonic Stopwatch (not DateTime) for sustainDuration and postSwitchBlackout so wall-clock jumps can't corrupt countdowns
A route switch requires candidateOffset + switchMarginMeters < bestOffset AND heading agreement > 0.3 AND sustained >= sustainDuration AND not within postSwitchBlackout
Candidate route snap/progress must never be folded into the emitted ActiveRouteState metrics until an actual switch has occurred (active-route metrics only)
EKF StationSnapConfirmed is accepted only if stationIndex > _lastEkfSnapIndex (ARM-side monotonic gate, §24.2); resetStationSnapIndex must be called on route change/session start

RouteSessionManager.clearSession must clear every per-route map (routeEventsByKey, stepBoundsMetersByKey, stepStopsCumulativeByKey, stepDurationsSecondsByKey, firstTransitBoardingByKey, transitModeByKey, transitLegStopsByKey, payloads) plus registry, or stale legs leak into the next session
Progress and boundaries are always in cumulative meters from route start; ETA is seconds
gotchas: DirectionService in-memory cache is keyed by the ACTUAL transitVariant/departureTime used, NOT the requestKey: a time-anchored metro-fallback route (transitVariant='subway', departureTime=next 09:00 local) is intentionally NOT served to a plain non-anchored request. RouteSessionManager, however, always builds its key with transitVariant='rail' for transit mode — so the session key can differ from the direction fetch's cache key.

getDirections retries exactly once on any exception by recursing with forceRefresh:true; a second failure throws. preferMetroEvenIfClosed makes a whole second API call and promoteRouteToFront reorders routes so index 0 is the chosen metro route.
buildRawSegments / buildSegmentedPolylines / RouteLogger._extractSummary only ever read routes[0] and its legs[0] — alternative routes are ignored once promoteRouteToFront has run.

TransitLegStops.fromJson silently 'heals' numStops: when isActualPositions && stopPositions non-empty it overrides declared numStops with stopPositions.length, so persisted numStops is not authoritative.

legId getter contains print()/emoji debug logging (🔑/⚠️) that fires on the hot path in production builds; its priority chain is metro stopNames > 'Walk to ' prefix (meters-based) > geometry lat/lng > meters fallback — changing any input silently changes the id and can re-fire per-leg alarms.
isTestMode drastically shortens ActiveRouteManager/DeviationMonitor/ReroutePolicy timings (e.g. sustain 6s->300ms, switchMargin 50m->20m, blackout 5s->300ms); behavior differs between tests and prod.

ActiveRouteManager, DeviationMonitor, ReroutePolicy are created lazily (??=) on the first registerRoute; the first registered route auto-becomes active only while !activeRouteInitialized. registerRoute also dedupes switchPoints within 200m of each other or within 200m of the destination.

RouteLogger is a singleton with enabled=true by default and writes the FULL raw Directions response (including origin/destination coords) as pretty JSON to the app documents dir on every successful fetch — unbounded growth and PII on disk; all failures are swallowed and return null.
_headingAgreement is a stub: it only checks that progress is non-regressing and returns a nominal 0.5 (no real gyro/compass), so route-switch heading gating is weak.

RouteEventBoundary.type is a bare string 'transfer' | 'mode_change' (no enum); consumers must string-match. TransitLegStops/RouteEventBoundary and per-route maps are hand-serialized via toJson/fromJson for the foreground-isolate/persistence round-trip, so any new field must be added in three places (fields, toJson, fromJson).

RouteSessionManager is imported by exactly one non-test file (trackingservice.dart) — it is the single owner; do not instantiate a second one. TransferUtils by contrast is a pure static toolbox imported by 49 files, so signature changes there ripple widely.

It is the "edge" of the app: everything that talks to the network, the OS, the sensors, or the simulation harness, and the shared transit-geometry utilities that the other three units consume. It fits between the screens/dashboards and the tracking/alarm/routing engines as their supplier of raw data (directions JSON, positions, notifications) and their platform integration layer.

Offline routing for simulation only: testing/OsmGraph + OsmLoader (.wkp binaries) + Pathfinder/DeviationPathfinder A* used by deviation dashboards
Abstractions & test doubles: PositionProvider/GpsPositionProvider scaffolding and TestServiceInstance fake ServiceInstance

feature: dev-tooling (developer/QA simulation & EKF-replay dashboards, Flutter-web only)
purpose: A collection of Flutter-web-only developer/QA dashboards for exercising WakePoint's tracking, deviation/reroute, and EKF dead-reckoning logic without walking a real metro route. It combines active GPS simulation (OSM-pathfinding deviations, time-warp up to 200x), passive monitoring of a real device over a WebSocket relay, EKF route-replay panels, and a typed constraint-event log rendered in a slide-out drawer. It is dev tooling, not end-user UI — none of it ships in the mobile app (it depends on dart:html) — but its ConstraintLogger event bus is also imported by production deviation/reroute services, so the unit is not fully isolated from shipping code.
responsibilities: Drive a Google-Maps dashboard that simulates GPS movement, route deviations, and returns via OSM pathfinding (DeviationSimulationController + osm_graph/pathfinder)
Provide global time-warp control (1x-200x) via TimeWarpSlider -> AppClock, so virtual time replaces wall-clock for all timestamps
Collect, stream, and display typed simulation/reroute events (ConstraintLogger singleton + ConstraintDrawer log viewer with JSON/CSV export)
Enforce a validated simulation lifecycle state machine (SimulationStateMachine: idle/onRoute/deviating/returning/paused)
Host EKF QA panels that replay recorded IMU/route data with GPS-dropout toggles (ekf_test_panel via imu_replay_engine_v2, ekf_replay_panel via imu_replay_engine)
Connect to the playground WebSocket relay (PlaygroundBridgeConfig.relayUrl) to monitor/broadcast real device state
Render OSM road overlays on the map with per-road-type styling (OsmOverlayManager)

Core simulation engine; emits SimulationTickResult per tick, computes deviation/return paths over osm_graph+pathfinder, delegates warpFactor to AppClock and logs ConstraintEvents
SimulationStateMachine (importers=7) with a whitelisted transition table over SimulationState; throws StateError on invalid transitions
Alternate standalone dashboard app (DeviationDashboardApp) that subscribes to ConstraintLogger.eventStream and rebroadcasts events to WebSocket clients

Processing: DeviationSimulationController ticks -> computes deviation/return paths via osm_graph + pathfinder, stamps virtualTime = AppClock().now(), and returns SimulationTickResult{position,heading,speedMps,virtualTime,distanceFromRoute}; every notable step logs a ConstraintEvent to ConstraintLogger.instance.log(). Outputs: ConstraintLogger.eventStream (broadcast) -> ConstraintDrawer renders it and deviation_dashboard forwards it to WebSocket clients; SimulationTickResult -> Google Maps markers/polylines on the dashboard. In parallel, ekf_test_panel/ekf_replay_panel replay IMU data (imu_replay_engine_v2 / imu_replay_engine) through EkfTestController and emit EkfReplayVisualization overlays. Production path: lib/services/deviation_monitor.dart and lib/services/reroute_policy.dart independently push ConstraintEvents into the same ConstraintLogger.instance.
usedBy: lib/main_unified_dashboard.dart (-> unified_dashboard.dart, the committed dev entrypoint)
invariants: ConstraintLogger is a private-constructor process-wide singleton (ConstraintLogger._ / .instance); all dashboard AND production callers share one event list and one broadcast eventStream. Use resetForTesting() to clear between tests.

AppClock is the single source of (possibly warped) time: ConstraintEvent.timestamp and SimulationTickResult.virtualTime are AppClock().now(), NOT wall-clock. warpFactor lives on the AppClock singleton.

SimulationStateMachine._transition only allows whitelisted (from,to) pairs and (_ -> idle); any other transition throws StateError — callers must respect the table and re-entrant same-state calls are no-ops.
eventController and stateController are broadcast StreamControllers and must be dispose()d; DeviationSimulationController/dashboards own their lifecycle.
Time-warp changes are global side effects: setWarpFactor mutates the shared AppClock, affecting any code in the isolate that reads AppClock().now().
gotchas: constraint_logger.dart is NOT purely dev tooling — it is the unit's highest-fan-in file (importers=10) and is imported+written by production services lib/services/deviation_monitor.dart and lib/services/reroute_policy.dart. Running the dashboard mutates global production singletons: UnifiedDashboard.initState sets TrackingService.isTestMode=true and TrackingService().setSimulationMode(true) — it reconfigures the real tracking service, not a sandboxed copy.

The time-warp slider warps a process-wide clock (AppClock().setWarpFactor). Because production timestamps also read AppClock().now(), warp leaks into anything sharing the AppClock singleton in the same isolate.

Two overlapping dashboard apps exist: UnifiedDashboard (has the committed main via lib/main_unified_dashboard.dart) and DeviationDashboard/DeviationDashboardApp (standalone app root with NO committed main wrapper). ConstraintLogger._events is append-only (log() only appends; only clear()/resetForTesting reset it) — long-running dashboard/relay sessions grow it unbounded.

purpose: The `lib/config/` unit is WakePoint's centralized tuning-constants and feature-flag layer. It holds the magic numbers for the deviation/reroute/termination pipeline (DeviationConfig), the battery-tier GPS/notification power profiles (PowerPolicy/PowerPolicyManager), the simulation/playground bridge gate (PlaygroundBridgeConfig), server endpoint/bundle-id constants (AppConfig), and the "am I running under flutter test" detector (detectFlutterTest). It is a pure leaf/source unit: everything here is stateless static const or immutable value objects that downstream tracking, dashboard, and networking code reads to make runtime decisions. It exists so tuning constants live in one place instead of being scattered across the tracking services.

Map a battery level (0-100%) to an immutable location/power profile: accuracy, distanceFilter, gpsDropoutBuffer, notificationTick, rerouteCooldown (PowerPolicyManager.forBatteryLevel / PowerPolicy.testing)
Gate whether the simulation WebSocket mirror is allowed to connect and expose the relay URL, defaulting OFF in release and under test (PlaygroundBridgeConfig)
Provide canonical server base URL and app bundle id constants that must stay aligned with the native build files and geowake-server (AppConfig)
Detect the flutter-test environment via a platform-conditional import so unit tests stay hermetic (detectFlutterTest, io vs stub)
Provide a cross-isolate file-based test-mode flag (TestModeFlag) — currently orphaned/unused

purpose: The geowake-server Node/Express backend is a thin, stateless API gateway that sits between the geowake2 Flutter app and the Google Maps Platform. Its whole reason to exist is to keep the Google Maps API key off the device: the phone never calls Google directly — it authenticates to this server with a device JWT, and the server proxies Directions/Autocomplete/Place-Details/Geocoding/Nearby-Search calls, injecting the secret key server-side and caching responses. It also mints the device tokens and enforces rate limiting. It holds no database and no user model; identity is just "is this request coming from our app bundle."
responsibilities: Mint short-lived (24h) device JWTs for clients that present the correct app bundle ID (POST /api/auth/token)
Verify Bearer JWTs on protected routes and reject expired/invalid/wrong-bundle tokens (authenticateDevice middleware)
Proxy 5 Google Maps endpoints, appending config.googleMapsApiKey server-side so the key never ships in the app
Cache Google Maps responses by structured type+params key with per-type TTLs (node-cache singleton)
Enforce per-route rate limiting and progressive slow-down keyed on client IP (x-forwarded-for)
Compose the Express app: security headers (helmet), CORS for mobile, compression, morgan logging, JSON body parsing, 404 + global error handlers, graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown
Validate required env (GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET>=32 chars) at boot and hard-exit if absent

(1) Token mint: Flutter api_client.dart POSTs /api/auth/token {bundleId:'com.geowake.app'} -> slowDownRules.general (server.js) -> rateLimitRules.auth (routes/auth.js) -> authController.generateToken checks bundleId===config.appBundleId -> jwt.sign({bundleId,iss:'GeoWake-Server'}, config.jwtSecret, {expiresIn:'24h'}) -> {success,token,expiresIn}. gotchas: Bundle ID mismatch trap: config default appBundleId is 'com.geowake.app' and the Flutter client sends 'com.geowake.app', but geowake-server/test/auth.test.js asserts success for 'com.yourcompany.geowake2' — tests only pass if APP_BUNDLE_ID env is set to that value. Three different bundle IDs exist across the repo.

authController.generateToken signs ONLY {bundleId, iss} — no deviceId/appVersion. But middleware/auth.js reads decoded.deviceId and decoded.appVersion into req.device, so req.device.id and req.device.appVersion are ALWAYS undefined for real tokens. The auth.js generateDeviceToken() helper that WOULD populate them is exported but never wired to any route (effectively dead).

cacheTimeouts only defines keys directions/places/geocoding. Handler types 'place-details' and 'nearby-search' have NO matching key, so cache.set falls back to 300s default silently — not the intended per-type TTL.

Successful proxy responses are returned as Google's raw JSON (res.json(response.data)) with no {success:true} wrapper; only errors get {success:false}. Clients must parse Google's native envelope (e.g. status:'OK', results/predictions), not a uniform success flag.
config.allowedOrigins defaults to include '*', so CORS is effectively open — do NOT treat CORS as the security boundary; JWT + bundleId is the only real gate.

cache.js exports a singleton that starts a setInterval stats logger that is never cleared, and rate-limit/slow-down keep timers too — Jest will report open handles / hang without --forceExit or teardown.

handleRateLimitError is largely unreachable: createRateLimit already supplies a custom handler that sends the 429 response, so the RateLimitExceeded error never propagates to this error-handling middleware.

No app.set('trust proxy'): limiters manually read x-forwarded-for to compensate, but express-rate-limit may still warn and req.ip fallback is unreliable unless deployed behind the expected single proxy hop.
